claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during solidification.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 displays multistep crystallization upon reheating.
An isothermal hold at approximately Tg - 10 K for about 1 minute immediately after rapid quenching is the proposed intervention.
The post-quench isothermal hold will promote structural relaxation in the amorphous matrix.
The post-quench isothermal hold will reduce free volume.
The hold will produce a more homogenized amorphous structure.
A relaxed, reduced-free-volume amorphous structure will resist nucleation and growth of crystalline phases.
Atomic rearrangement and relaxation during the hold will lower the driving force for primary crystallization.
Structural stabilization caused by the hold will inhibit formation of critical crystalline nuclei.
Inhibiting critical nuclei will delay crystallization during reheating.
The intervention will yield a higher retained amorphous volume fraction than conventional processing.
The intervention will shift the onset of primary crystallization exotherms upward by more than 5 K.
Standard rapidly solidified Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits extensive primary crystallization.
Standard rapidly solidified Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has lower crystallization-onset temperatures and reduced thermal stability relative to the proposed treatment.
The beneficial effect is contingent on an initial rapid-cooling rate greater than 10^5 K/s.
The beneficial effect is contingent on holding within approximately 10 K below Tg.
The beneficial effect is contingent on reheating at less than 50 K/min.
